summary: William Stede worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at SOAS University of London (~1928–1930) and the University of London (~1928–1949), and taught George Peiris Malalasekera, Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera, and E. W. Adikaram.

William Theodore de Bary worked in Sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (1937–1953) and Harvard University (~1941–1942), and served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia University (~1953–1990), where he taught Bettine Birge.

William Van Gordon is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and has held a post as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University.

William Wilson Hunter worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at The Glasgow Academy, University of Glasgow, and the universities of Paris and Bonn. He held posts in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1887) and University of Calcutta (~1886–1887).

William Woodville Rockhill worked in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at Lycée Condorcet and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and later served at the United States Legation in Peking (~1884–1888).

William Wright was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at the University of St Andrews (~1845–1849). He held posts at University College London, the British Museum (~1861–1870), and the University of Cambridge (1887–1888).

Willibald Kirfel specialized in Indology, studying at the University of Bonn (~1904–1908) under Hermann Jacobi. In 1920, he served at the University of Bonn as Bibliothekar und Privatdozent and also succeeded Hermann Jacobi.

Wilt L. Idema is a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University (~1963–1974) under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé. He was a professor at Leiden (1975–1999), director at Harvard University (2000), and a fellow at the Radcliffe Institute (2001–2002).

Winfred Robert Martin worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College (~1888–1907) and later as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America (~1907–1915).

Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan studied at Cornell University (~1970–1974). She taught at Washington and Lee University (~1994–2000), served as Dean of Students and Senior Lecturer at the University of Chicago (~2000–2005), and held a post at Indiana University (~2012).

Winston Kyan specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1999–2006) under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung, and also studied under Donald Harper and Linda Seidel.

Sinologist Wolfgang Kubin studied at the universities of Münster (~1966–1967), Vienna (~1967–1969), and Ruhr University Bochum (~1969–1973). He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (~1977–1985) and the University of Bonn (~1985–2011), where he taught Carmen Meinert.

Wolfgang Morgenroth worked in Indology and linguistics, earning his PhD at the University of Jena (~1953–1958) under Richard Hauschild and Karl Ammer. He later held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1976–1995) and the University of Potsdam (2020).

Wolfram Eberhard worked in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1927–1933) and held posts at Ankara University (~1937–1948) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1948–1976).

Woncheol Yun specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Stony Brook University (~-1989) and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (~1990–2021).

Woosung Huh works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Hawaii (~-1988) and served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (~1991–2018).

Wu Hung is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Harvard University (~1980–1987). Beginning around 1994, he held posts as Professor at the University of Chicago and at the Smart Museum of Art.
Wulstan Fletcher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche.

Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (~2011–2016). Xianda studied under K. L. Dhammajoti, Guang Xing, and Toshiichi Endo.

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua University (1930–1934) and the University of Göttingen (1935–1941). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (1937) and Peking University (1946–1980).
